merger_description:
The acquirer is a special purpose vehicle, majority owned by KKR Forge Aggregator L.P. (**KKR Aggregator**), a newly-formed investment vehicle advised and managed by KKR.

KKR is a global investment firm that offers alternative asset management as well as capital markets and insurance solutions. KKR sponsors investment funds that invest in private equity, credit, and real assets and has strategic partners that manage hedge funds.

Crowe LLP (**Crowe**) is a global independent accounting and advisory firm, currently controlled by the Crowe LLP partners (**Crowe Partners**), which operates across four business units: advisory, audit, consulting and tax. Crowe is a member of Crowe Global, a global network of professional service providers.

In Australia, Findex (Aust) Pty Ltd, trading as Crowe Australasia, provides attestation, tax, and consulting services. Findex (Aust) Pty Ltd is a leading provider of integrated financial advisory and accounting services in Australia.

KKR has agreed to acquire 45% of the equity interests in the advisory, tax and consulting business of Crowe (held by Crowe ParentCo LLC), together with a consortium of co-investors who have agreed to acquire an indirect minority 10% equity interest (the **Acquisition**). Following completion of the Acquisition, KKR will hold 45% of the equity interest, the consortium of co-investors will hold 10% and Crowe will retain the remaining 45% of the equity interests.

determination_table_content.details:
Forge Merger Sub LLC, a special purpose vehicle which is majority
owned, advised and managed by KKR, applied for a notification
waiver in respect of its proposed acquisition of share capital in
Crowe ParentCo LLC, which will hold the advisory, tax and consulting
business of Crowe LLP (Crowe), as described in the transaction
documents provided as part of the application (the Acquisition).
KKR has agreed to acquire 45% of the equity interests in the
advisory, tax and consulting business of Crowe, together with a
consortium of co-investors who have agreed to acquire an indirect
minority 10% equity interest. Following completion of the
Acquisition, KKR will hold 45% of the equity interest, the consortium
of co-investors will hold 10% and Crowe will retain the remaining
45% of the equity interests.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

KKR is a global investment firm that offers alternative asset
management as well as capital markets and insurance solutions.
KKR sponsors investment funds that invest in private equity, credit,
and real assets and has strategic partners that manage hedge funds.
Crowe is a global independent accounting and advisory firm,
currently controlled by the Crowe LLP Partners. Crowe operates
across four business units globally: advisory, audit, consulting and
tax. In Australia, Crowe only provides tax and consulting services.
Findex (Aust) Pty Ltd, trading as Crowe Australasia, also provides
attestation, tax, and consulting services in Australia. Findex (Aust)
Pty Ltd is a leading provider of integrated financial advisory and
accounting services.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. In particular, there is no horizontal overlap
or vertical relationships between the parties or their connected
entities in Australia.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
